anchors.90-100: No errors; succinct, precise medical register; appropriate abbreviations used correctly
anchors.70-80: Occasional minor errors; does not impair clinical communication
anchors.30-40: Frequent errors; impairs clarity of presentation

anchors.90-100: All clinical data and interpretations accurate; correct medical terminology throughout
anchors.50-60: Some clinical inaccuracies or terminology errors
anchors.30-40: Multiple clinical errors; interpretation errors present
anchors.10-20: Significant clinical errors compromising patient safety

anchors.90-100: Succinct, structured, prioritized presentation; clear assessment with differential; logical plan
anchors.70-80: Good structure; assessment and plan present; minor gaps
anchors.50-60: Adequate structure but key elements missing or poorly organized
anchors.10-20: Severely disorganized; unable to follow clinical reasoning

anchors.90-100: Confident, well-paced delivery; no notes dependency; fielded questions smoothly
anchors.70-80: Mostly fluent; occasional reference to notes; good question handling
anchors.30-40: Frequent hesitation; poor pacing; difficulty answering questions

anchors.90-100: Exceptional empathy and professionalism; creates psychological safety
anchors.70-80: Good empathy; acknowledges emotion; polite and professional
anchors.50-60: Adequate but mechanical empathy; some emotional cues missed
anchors.30-40: Little empathic response; information delivery prioritized
anchors.10-20: No empathic response; dismissive or unprofessional

checklist.item: patient demographics and one-liner (age, sex, presenting complaint)
relevant positives and negatives from history
clear assessment: primary diagnosis stated first
management plan presented in logical order
presentation under 3 minutes without being asked to shorten
used Teach-back method to verify patient understanding
